featured_reviews.name: beyondaverage
featured_reviews.review_text:
Staff is Extremely Rude and Arrogant

I honestly cannot believe the way I was treated at this general store. The staff here are unbelievably rude and have no sense of how to talk to customers. I was quietly checking out a few items, and out of nowhere one of them snapped at me saying, “Niklo yaha se, ghoomne nahi aate, jo lena hai woh lo aur niklo.”

I wasn’t wasting anyone’s time or causing any inconvenience—I was simply browsing like any normal customer. But the attitude I received was unacceptable. They made me feel as if I was doing something wrong just by being there.

This kind of arrogance and disrespect should not be tolerated in any business. You don’t open a shop to insult people. Customers deserve to be treated with basic courtesy and respect.

This was not just a bad experience—it was insulting. I will never step foot in this store again, and I’ll make sure others know how poorly they treat people. Taking further action is definitely on my list.

Highly disappointed and deeply offended.

featured_reviews.name: Glenn Dmello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a terrible experience with Urban Platter. I purchased boba and cake, which were completely inedible.

When I went back to the store to return them, Manager Vedant outright refused to take them back because they were “opened.” How else am I supposed to know if the products are bad without tasting them? Does Urban Platter expect customers to return sealed items without even checking if they’re fit for consumption?

The fact that I took the trouble to travel all the way back should have been proof enough that the products were substandard, yet the store refused to take responsibility. Urban Platter charges premium prices, but clearly, there is no quality control whatsoever. How do such terrible products even make it to the self. Horrible experience.

featured_reviews.name: Mridula Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Even though we live near Dadar, love coming here just to come to Food Square at Santacruz.

A lush, spacious offering of the best in fresh fruits, vegetables and everything from A-Z in the imported zone.

We love the tastings of the cheese, fresh assorted breads, fruits, guacamole, pasta. A visual tasting experience before buying the product adds a personal touch to make the right buying choice.

Though the prices are expensive, there is something for everyone.

The ground floor further accentuates into a dining experience provided from the Barn, Zinque Patisserie, and so much more.

Their cheese platters are the best. And they let you try cheese with crackers and fruit.

You get every exotic fruit and vegetable. The likes of Amalfi lemons which I held for the first time in my hand, and sundries tomatoes from Italy and Spain. Every corner leaves you stunned.

Also appreciate the ‘ancient grains’ millet space which has the healthiest amaranth, bajra, jowar,quinoa and you name it.

Always keep coming back to here, never knew that a grocery shopping space could be so therapeutic and feel good.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Mridula,
Appreciate your visit! Looking forward to serving you again soon.
Team,
Food square

featured_reviews.name: Anugraha Ghale
featured_reviews.review_text:
The store itself is actually pretty good. It’s clean, well laid out, and checkout is smooth because there are a lot of counters. That part works well and doesn’t feel chaotic.

The grocery section is strong. Fruits, chocolates, packaged items, and daily essentials were all good quality and available in proper quantity. I also noticed some good deals and discounts on a few products. If you’re coming here mainly for groceries, this place does the job well.

However, I really do not recommend buying clothes from this Reliance Smart store. Almost everything I saw was polyester or polyester blends. Even items that looked like cotton turned out to be mixed with polyester. I was genuinely disappointed because a market like India has access to such good fabrics, and I was hoping to find pure cotton, khadi, or more natural materials. That was not the case here at all.

I spent quite some time looking for better fabric options and eventually gave up. The clothing section felt like an afterthought and didn’t match the quality of the rest of the store.

Overall, good place for groceries and household items. Not a place I would visit for clothes.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Anugraha Ghale,Thanks for your review ! We are very happy to know you've been satisfied with your experience at SMART Bazaar.

We are looking forward to serve you again!

featured_reviews.name: Hersh Rijhsinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are a few areas that need improvement.

The AC needs attention, as it can get quite uncomfortable inside. The cash counter staff would also benefit from better training. I understand that there is often a lot of crowd, but with better management, the overall experience could be much smoother.

Another concern is that the discounts displayed on the racks often do not match the final billing amount, which can be confusing and frustrating at checkout.

Due to these repeated issues, I have currently stopped visiting. I hope the management takes feedback seriously and works on these areas for a better customer experience.

featured_reviews.name: Kimberley Parker
featured_reviews.review_text: Terrible, They have more staff than customers at the store, who are completely unbothered! I placed an order at 2.30  pm for home delivery at 6 pm  I get a call from my 10th floor neighbour saying the delivery guy has mistakenly delivered at her place! Lucky she was home! Never mind they deliver to my place each week. No intimation that there would be a delay ,nothing, its for the customer to chase their royal highnesses. Then I noticed that the price of an item on the sticker was Rs. 666  but on the bill it was Rs. 715.  When I called them out they insisted it was a labelling mistake?  No one at this store wants to take accountability, the delivery boy insisted he had been given was incorrect, the lady at the counter insisted it was the delivery boys mistake, and so on and forth. So you know.. its not a good idea to disrespect customer time and money this way.  Certainly not in an uncertain economy.

featured_reviews.name: ramesh bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gangar stores is a family managed farsan and dry snack store. It has been rather popular with local residents of Santa Cruz west. It was revamped about 2-3 years ago and has been doing great since .

Located right next to an international school and junior college, it has a vast range of packaged foods, snacks, breads, pickles, khaakhraas, sauces, freshly made dips, Indian sweets, (mithaai and shrikhand) chips and even a few varieties of dry fruits and chocolates. During summer they also stock aamras i.e frozen mango pulp

Their dry snacks are some of the freshest you will find including sev puris, chaklis, puris for pani puri, and also fresh snacks like dhoklaas

There are 2 chemists, an all veg bakery and a much loved icecream parlour - Gokul  icecreams (reviewed by me earlier) just next door.

If you're a samosa lover, and you go there by mid morning, you can buy te famous A1 samosas!!

The staff are courteous and helpful

Credit card payment: yes
Parking: available outside the store
Wheelchair compliant: no
Washroom: no
Home delivery: no

The guy on the phone hung up on me twice and refused to answer a single question and talking with people in the store while keeping me on hold
Good for them that they are so busy and have so much business that they are turning customers away, the plenty of other grocery stores in the neighbourhood, who can do with new customers and new business.
In today’s day and age, you have to learn some public relations and some sort of humility. Otherwise, your business is not going to survive
